Repeat the diagnostic with several values of seed

Source: R/seed_sensitivity.R
seed_sensitivity.Rd

The fold split and every tree model of propensity_sensitivity() depend on seed, and on small data the kept models and the summaries can change noticeably from one seed to the next. seed_sensitivity() reruns propensity_sensitivity() once per value of seeds (here: values of its seed argument) with every other argument unchanged, and returns one row per seed with the models kept, whether the gate fell back, and the main summaries, plus their range. Report the whole table.

Usage

seed_sensitivity(x, seeds = 1:3, ..., model_seeds = NULL, keep_results = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'seed_sensitivity'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

x

A matchit object or a two-sided formula, as for propensity_sensitivity().

seeds

Values of seed to run (default 1:3). Each value is one full run.

...

Further arguments for propensity_sensitivity() (for example data, algorithms, replace, caliper, cores), except seed.

model_seeds

The seeds argument of propensity_sensitivity() (the number of seeds per tree algorithm, as 1:k); NULL (default) keeps its default 1:3.

keep_results

TRUE to keep every full result in results (large); default FALSE.

digits

Significant digits for printed numbers.

Value

An object of class "seed_sensitivity": a list with table (one row per seed: seed, models_kept, models_fitted, algorithms_kept, kept_by_algorithm, fallback, rank_disagreement, rank_disagreement_equal_weight, pair_instability, bootstrap_rank_instability), range (minimum and maximum of each summary over the seeds) and results (NULL unless keep_results = TRUE).

Details

The R warnings of each run about the gate fallback and about a single kept algorithm are not repeated; they are columns of the table (fallback, algorithms_kept).

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
by_seed <- seed_sensitivity(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75, seeds = 1:2,
  data = lalonde, algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting"),
  model_seeds = 1, n_trees = 50, bootstrap_samples = 2
)
by_seed
#> Propensity model sensitivity over 2 values of `seed`
#>  seed models_kept models_fitted algorithms_kept
#>     1           3             3               3
#>     2           3             3               3
#>                                            kept_by_algorithm fallback
#>  logistic regression 1, random forest 1, gradient boosting 1     TRUE
#>  logistic regression 1, random forest 1, gradient boosting 1     TRUE
#>  rank_disagreement rank_disagreement_equal_weight pair_instability
#>             0.0692                         0.0692            0.659
#>             0.0677                         0.0677            0.659
#>  bootstrap_rank_instability
#>                      0.0230
#>                      0.0348
#> 
#> Range over the seeds:
#>                         summary minimum maximum
#>               rank_disagreement  0.0677  0.0692
#>  rank_disagreement_equal_weight  0.0677  0.0692
#>                pair_instability  0.6590  0.6590
#>      bootstrap_rank_instability  0.0230  0.0348
#> Some seeds fell back to every model or kept a single algorithm; their values
#>    do not describe a set of similarly good models from several algorithms.
#> Report every row; the values depend on the seed as much as shown here.
